title: BUG: GroupBy.agg with as_index=False and MultiIndex column grouping key raises ValueError
body:
## Automated contributions disclosure

I used an automated tool to develop this pull request.

- **Tool / harness:** `opencode` (open-source coding agent CLI), running under Claude Code.
- **Model:** `big-pickle` (model ID `opencode/big-pickle`).
- **Reasoning-effort / thinking setting:** this tool and model do not expose a user-selectable effort or thinking setting, so none applies. OpenCode does not publish a separate dated snapshot for this model, so the model ID above is the most specific identifier available.
- **How I used it, and what it produced:**
  - Explored the `as_index=False` + `MultiIndex`-columns code path and located the failing `_insert_inaxis_grouper` branch.
  - Drafted the change to `full_key()` and the membership check in `pandas/core/groupby/groupby.py`.
  - Wrote the two new tests in `pandas/tests/groupby/`.
  - Ran the test suites and the `ruff` checks recorded under **Verification** below.
  - Wrote the initial draft of this description, which I then reviewed, corrected, and rewrote in my own words.
  - Everything reproduced above was re-derived by me: I ran the reproduction script, confirmed the pre-fix `ValueError` and the post-fix output, reviewed every changed line, and confirmed the behaviour matches the canonical `as_index=True` + `reset_index()` form.

I reviewed and understand every change in this PR, and the commit messages are my own. I can explain the reasoning for each change on request.

---
Closes GH-39103

---

### Reproduction

```python
df = pd.DataFrame({("col0", "l0"): [0, 0, 1], ("col1", "l1"): [10, 20, 30]})
df.groupby(("col0", "l0"), as_index=False).agg({("col1", "l1"): ["min", "max"]})
```

```text
ValueError: Item must have length equal to number of levels.
```

### Root cause

`_insert_inaxis_grouper` in `pandas/core/groupby/groupby.py` decides whether the `as_index=False` group key has already been inserted by the aggregation itself. For a `MultiIndex` columns frame, the str-name path pads the key to the columns' `nlevels` (`("key", "", ...)`, per GH-17024 / GH-28549), but a tuple name of fewer levels than `result.columns.nlevels` was returned unchanged, and `result.insert(0, name, lev)` then failed with the "Item must have length equal to number of levels" `ValueError`.

### Fix

`full_key()` now also pads tuple names when `len(name) < result.columns.nlevels`, and the membership check uses `full_key(name)` so it looks up the exact key that will be inserted (previously a partial-tuple lookup which additionally raised `PerformanceWarning` on un-lex-sorted `MultiIndex` columns, surfaced as an error under CI's `filterwarnings`).

The inserted grouper column now exactly matches the canonical `groupby(..., as_index=True).agg(...).reset_index()` output.

### Verification

- Issue repro now returns the expected padded columns `[("col0", "l0", ""), ("col1", "l1", "min"), ("col1", "l1", "max")]`, byte-identical to the `as_index=True` + `reset_index()` form for `agg`, `describe`, and multi-tuple-grouper cases
- New tests: `test_groupby_agg_as_index_false_multiindex_column` (padded columns, existing column order, empty input) and `test_groupby_as_index_false_multiindex_column_matches_reset_index` (agg/describe/multi-tuple equivalence)
- `pandas/tests/groupby/`: 24447 passed, 866 skipped, 43 xfailed
- Sweep of `pandas/tests/resample/`, `pandas/tests/apply/`, `pandas/tests/reshape/`: green (2 unrelated pre-existing tzdata DST failures, confirmed identical on `main`)
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean (repo-pinned ruff 0.16.6); `aggregate/` suite green under `-W error`

title: BUG: fix DataFrame.join with list when indexes have different levels (#57676)
body:
- [x] closes #57676
- [x] tests added / passed
- [x] Ensure all linting tests pass

When passing a list to \DataFrame.join\, it tries to optimize by falling back to \pd.concat(axis=1)\ if all indexes are unique. However, \concat\ does not support broadcasting across mismatched MultiIndex levels, leading to a \NotImplementedError\ or incorrect results if names differ.

This commit updates the \can_concat\ heuristic in \DataFrame.join\ to ensure that if any frame's index is a \MultiIndex\, all frames must have exactly identical index names (and therefore matching structures) in order to use the \concat\ fast-path. Otherwise, it gracefully falls back to iteratively calling \merge\, which correctly handles broadcasting and subset MultiIndex joins.

Adds a `bias` parameter to `Series.skew`, `Series.kurt`, `DataFrame.skew`, and `DataFrame.kurt`, matching the convention used by `scipy.stats.skew` and `scipy.stats.kurtosis`. Defaults to `False`, which preserves current (bias-corrected/sample) behavior — this is a non-breaking change.

The underlying computation is added at the Cython level in `calc_skew`/`calc_kurt` (`pandas/_libs/algos.pxd`), threaded up through `nanops.nanskew`/`nankurt`, and exposed on `Series`/`DataFrame`.

Scope note: `Rolling`/`Expanding.skew()`/`.kurt()` and `GroupBy.skew()`/`.kurt()` are intentionally left out of this PR — they use separate call paths, and `GroupBy` currently has an active deprecation blocking new kwargs. Happy to open follow-up issues for those if maintainers want them.

title: Fix/parallel read csv converters
body:
Closes #68505

### Summary

Keep user-defined `converters` eligible for parallel `read_csv`, but turn thread-affinity failures from converter worker threads into an actionable error.

Most converters are safe to run in parser workers. A converter that captures a thread-affine resource, such as a SQLite connection created on the caller thread, cannot safely use that resource from a worker thread.

### Changes

* Keep the existing parallel-read eligibility rules; do not blanket-disable parallel parsing for `converters`.
* Detect common thread-affinity error messages raised by converter worker threads.
* Re-raise those failures with guidance to use a thread-safe resource or set `mode.max_threads=1`.
* Add a regression test using SQLite for the motivating case from GH#68505.
* Add a v3.1.0 whatsnew entry.

### Testing

* `git diff --check` was verified on the prepared branch.
* The focused pytest could not be executed in the Windows environment because the pandas C extensions are not built (`pandas._libs.pandas_parser` is unavailable).

`Index._intersection` deduplicates the libjoin merge result with PyArrow's hash
kernel. The merge emits its keys in order, so the duplicates are already adjacent
and run-end encoding collapses them in one pass, no hash table needed. Same
direction as #14273, which #64646 applied to `Index.get_indexer`.

This brings up to ~6x on large all-unique Arrow numeric indexes, ~1.7–2.4x on the more realistic partial-overlap shape, and ~1.2–1.6x for Arrow strings. The only regression happens with signed-zero, around 15%. But that is a rare use case.

title: BUG preserve Arrow scalar arithmetic dtypes (GH#69436)
body:
Closes #69436

Arrow-backed Series arithmetic can widen results when a Python scalar is inferred as a wider Arrow type than the array. This change preserves the array dtype when the scalar and result fit, while retaining wider results when arithmetic overflows or needs a wider type.

The implementation keeps float calculations on the original scalar before narrowing the result, so scalar conversion does not lose small or large values. Decimal results are narrowed only when they can be represented by the input decimal type.

Tests cover integer scalar arithmetic, overflow promotion, float scalar edge cases, decimal arithmetic, and the reported reproductions.

back:

```python
>>> idx = pd.date_range("2020-01-01", periods=8, freq="SME")
>>> pd.infer_freq(idx)
None
```

`_infer_daily_rule` tries annual, then quarterly, then monthly, then the daily
rules. A semi-monthly index has two distinct deltas, so `mdiffs` has more than
one element and `_get_monthly_rule` bails; `is_unique` is False so the daily
rules are skipped; and it falls through to `None`. Semi-monthly was never in the
chain.

This adds `_get_semi_monthly_rule` between the monthly and daily steps. It
matches the two anchor patterns, day 1 and 15 for `SMS`, day 15 and month end
for `SME`, and then requires that the anchors strictly alternate, advancing one
month each time the day of month drops back:

```python
nmonths = (self.fields["Y"] * 12 + self.fields["M"]).astype("i8")
rolls_over = (days[1:] < days[:-1]).astype("i8")
if not np.array_equal(np.diff(nmonths), rolls_over):
    return None
```

That alternation check is what keeps the rule conservative. Cases that must not
be claimed, all verified to still return `None`:

| index | result |
| --- | --- |
| `2SME` (months advance two at a time) | `None` |
| 1st and 15th, but a month repeats | `None` |
| day 15 paired with day 20 rather than month end | `None` |
| `MS` alone, or `ME` alone | `MS` / `ME` as before |

Verified across the full anchor set, so nothing else changed: `ME`, `MS`, `D`,
`h`, `B`, `QE-DEC`, `YE-DEC` and `W-SUN` all still round trip, and `SME`/`SMS`
now do too, from either anchor as the start point. Leap-year February is handled,
since the `SME` anchor is month end rather than a fixed day.

#### Testing

`pandas/tests/tseries/` and `test_date_range.py`: 8293 passed, 3 skipped,
2 xfailed. Seven of the new tests fail on `main` and pass here. All pre-commit
hooks pass, including the whatsnew alphabetical-ordering hook.

### Description

Sorting a DataFrame containing columns with PyArrow `null` type (e.g. `df.sort_values(list(df.columns))`) raised `ValueError: Categorical categories cannot be null`.

#### Root Cause
When sorting multiple columns, `DataFrame.sort_values` uses `lexsort_indexer`, which factorizes columns via `factorize(use_na_sentinel=True)` and creates `Categorical` from the resulting codes and categories. For `pa.null()`, `pa.chunked_array.dictionary_encode(null_encoding="mask")` produces a dictionary of null type containing a null element (`[<NA>]`). Because `use_na_sentinel=True` was passed, returning null categories violated the `CategoricalDtype` invariant that categories cannot contain nulls. This also caused `pd.Categorical(s)` and `s.astype("category")` to fail on `null[pyarrow]` Series.

#### Fix
In `ArrowExtensionArray.factorize`, handle `pa.types.is_null(data.type)`:
- When `use_na_sentinel=True` or array is empty: return sentinel indices (`-1`) and an empty chunked array with `pa.null()` as `uniques`.
- When `use_na_sentinel=False`: return `0` indices and `uniques` containing a single null scalar `[None]` with `pa.null()`.

#### AI Disclosure
Drafted with Google Antigravity using Gemini 3.8 Flash (High), following `AGENTS.md`. The workflow reproduced the issue, implemented the fix in `ArrowExtensionArray.factorize`, added regression and unit tests in `pandas/tests/extension/test_arrow.py`, added a release note in `doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst`, verified code formatting with ruff, and verified that all existing and new test suites pass.

title: BUG: groupby.rank with Arrow string dtype (#59088)
body:
Closes #59088

### What does this PR do?
ArrowExtensionArray._groupby_op fell through to _to_masked() for string and large_string Arrow dtypes. _to_masked has no conversion for strings and raises NotImplementedError, which the groupby machinery surfaces as:
```text
TypeError: rank is not supported for string[pyarrow] dtype
TypeError: rank is not supported for large_string[pyarrow] dtype
```
This PR routes how == "rank" through a python-backed StringArray before that fallback, so rank runs through the existing cython/numpy implementation. Reductions (sum, first, last, any, all, idxmin, idxmax, ...) are unaffected — their code path is unchanged.

### Example
Previously:
```python
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow as pa

df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "key": [1, 1, 2, 2],
        "value": pd.arrays.ArrowExtensionArray(
            pa.array(["b", "a", "d", "c"], type=pa.string())
        ),
    }
)
df.groupby("key")["value"].rank()
```
raised:
```text
TypeError: rank is not supported for string[pyarrow] dtype
```
### After this change:
returns:

```text
0    2.0
1    1.0
2    2.0
3    1.0
Name: value, dtype: float64
```
The same works for pa.large_string() and honors method, ascending, and na_option, matching the result for pandas' "string" dtype using lexicographic ordering.

### Changes
- Added a how == "rank" branch to ArrowExtensionArray._groupby_op that builds a python-storage StringArray and delegates to its _groupby_op for string and large_string Arrow dtypes.
- Added a StringArray import in pandas/core/arrays/arrow/array.py.
- Added regression tests test_rank_arrow_string_dtype and test_rank_arrow_string_dtype_with_na.
- Added a What's New entry under Groupby/resample/rolling.

### Testing
Added regression tests:
- test_rank_arrow_string_dtype (parametrized over pa.string() / pa.large_string(), method in {"average", "first"}, ascending in {True, False})
- test_rank_arrow_string_dtype_with_na

Targeted runs:
```text
pytest pandas/tests/groupby/methods/test_rank.py -k "arrow_string" -q
10 passed, 1548 deselected
```
```text
pytest pandas/tests/groupby/test_reductions.py::test_string_dtype_all_na -q
704 passed
```
Both tests fail with the original TypeError when the new branch is reverted, confirming they exercise the fix.

title: BUG preserve row alignment in grouped resampling on columns
body:
Fixes #59350, an existing report from 2024. This is a fix contribution, not a newly discovered upstream issue.

With the pandas 3.0.6 release, grouped resampling on a datetime column can silently assign values to the wrong time bins when row labels are a permutation of row positions:

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "group": ["a", "a", "b", "b"],
        "date": pd.date_range("2024-01-01", periods=4, freq="min"),
        "value": [100, 200, 1000, 2000],
    },
    index=[1, 0, 3, 2],
)
df.groupby("group").resample("1min", on="date").agg({"value": "sum"})
```

The observed values for group a are 200 then 100 instead of 100 then 200; group b is similarly reversed (2000 then 1000 instead of 1000 then 2000). The fix constructs each group's time grouper from that group's datetime values and avoids interpreting arbitrary row labels as positional offsets. Regression coverage exercises both dict aggregation and Series selection with permuted and arbitrary labels.

Validation: reproduced against the unmodified pandas 3.0.6 wheel. The equivalent fix applied to that wheel passes eight targeted regression/control cases (including ordinary resampling and index-/level-based group resampling); Ruff checks/format and Python compilation pass on this checkout. The source checkout lacks built C extensions, so its in-tree pytest module could not be loaded locally; CI is needed for full-tree validation. Prevalence and affected downstream analyses are unknown. The earlier #59408 PR was closed unmerged and does not cover this multi-group/custom-index reproduction.

title: BUG: fix read_csv pyarrow engine IndexError for dtype dict missing index_col (#68041)
body:
Closes #68041

## Summary
`read_csv` with `engine="pyarrow"` and `dtype_backend="pyarrow"` raised an
`IndexError` when `index_col` was given and a dict `dtype` did not name the
index column:

```python
pd.read_csv(f, dtype={"col2": "int64[pyarrow]"},
            dtype_backend="pyarrow", engine="pyarrow", index_col="col1")
```

In `ArrowParserWrapper._finalize_index`, the dtype-dict branch tried to look up
the index column via `frame.columns[item]`. That label lookup is only valid when
`item` is an integer position; for a string `index_col` missing from the dtype
dict it indexed the Arrow-backed column labels incorrectly and raised
`IndexError: only integers, slices ... are valid indices`.

The nested lookup is now restricted to the integer-`index_col` case (looking the
column name up by position in `frame.columns`). A string `index_col` that is
missing from the dtype dict is left to normal inference, and the remaining
`dtype` keys are applied afterwards in `_finalize_dtype`. A scalar dtype with
`index_col` (Scenario A) was already fixed by #66063 / #45801 and is unaffected.

title: BUG: merge with NaN-labeled join key produces duplicate columns
body:
## What does this fix

When merging two DataFrames on a column whose name is `NaN`, pandas incorrectly produces duplicate columns with suffixes (`nan_x`, `nan_y`) instead of recognizing the shared join key and keeping a single column.

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

left = pd.DataFrame({np.nan: [1, 2, 3], "a": [10, 20, 30]})
right = pd.DataFrame({np.nan: [1, 2, 3], "b": [40, 50, 60]})

pd.merge(left, right, left_on=np.nan, right_on=np.nan).columns
# Before: Index([nan, 'nan_x', 'a', 'nan_y', 'b'], dtype='str')
# After:  Index([nan, 'a', 'b'])
```

## Root cause

In `_get_merge_keys`, the right key column is dropped when `lk == rk`. But `np.nan == np.nan` is `False` in Python, so the right `NaN` column is never dropped. The existing code even has a `# FIXME: what about other NAs?` comment acknowledging this.

Similarly, `_should_fill` returns `True` unconditionally for non-string keys without checking if both are matching NAs.

## Fix

Use `is_matching_na` from `pandas._libs.missing` for NaN-aware equality:
1. In `_get_merge_keys`: `lk == rk or is_matching_na(lk, rk)` 
2. In `_should_fill`: return `is_matching_na(lname, rname) or lname == rname` for non-string keys

## Tests

Added two tests:
- `test_merge_nan_column_name_no_duplicates` — verifies the exact issue from #65899
- `test_merge_nan_column_name_on` — verifies the same fix works with `on=` parameter

Fixes #65899

title: BUG: numexpr results use a nonstandard int64 type, breaking select_dtypes (GH#17945)
body:
closes #17945

numexpr returns int64 results as `longlong` (`'q'`), whereas numpy's int64 is `long` (`'l'`) on Linux/macOS. The dtypes compare equal but `dtype.type is not np.int64`, so e.g. `select_dtypes("int64")` silently dropped the column. This hit `DataFrame.eval`/`pd.eval`, and also plain arithmetic/`where` on data large enough to be routed through numexpr.

Results from the three numexpr call sites are now viewed (no copy) as numpy's standard dtype when they differ.

Binary ufuncs without an operator equivalent (`np.logical_or`, `np.logaddexp`, ...) aligned their inputs by taking the union of the axes and calling `reindex`, which raises on duplicate labels. The other behavior in the issue (NaN for non-overlapping columns) is the intended alignment enforced in 2.0 (GH-39239).

title: BUG: read_sql with DBAPI cursors returning dict rows (GH#53028)
body:
closes #53028
closes #52437

Since 2.0, `read_sql`/`read_sql_query` on a DBAPI connection whose cursor returns rows as dicts (pymysql `DictCursor`, pymssql `as_dict=True`, a dict-building sqlite3 `row_factory`) filled every cell with its column name: `lib.to_object_array_tuples` turns each dict into a tuple of its keys. Dict rows are now converted with `tuple(row.values())`. This uses the cursor's column order rather than lookup by name, because pymysql renames duplicate join columns to `table.col`.

Tests: a sqlite dict `row_factory` test (with and without `chunksize`), and a `db`-marked test using a real pymysql `DictCursor`, as requested in review of the earlier attempt GH-63503.

title: BUG: convert non-native byteorder to native at construction (GH#53234)
body:
closes #53234

Non-native byteorder numeric data (e.g. `>f4` on a little-endian machine) was kept as-is by the Series/DataFrame/Index constructors, so anything reaching a Cython routine raised `ValueError: Big-endian buffer not supported on little-endian compiler` — Index lookups, unique/factorize/value_counts, take/reindex/merge, groupby, window ops, reductions, etc.

This converts to native byteorder at construction (block creation, `Index._ensure_array`, `pd.array` inference), like `DatetimeArray` already does and `Index` did in 1.5. Public functions that accept a raw ndarray (`pd.unique`, `pd.factorize`, `take`) also convert at their Cython boundary. The GH-43042 tests asserting the byteorder is preserved are updated to assert native dtypes with the same values. Also fixes `pd.array` raising `KeyError` on non-native input, and updates the byte-ordering section of the gotchas guide.

title: TYP: remove mode from BaseBuffer protocol (GH#60660)
body:
closes #60660

`BaseBuffer` required a `mode` property, so objects like `io.IOBase` and botocore's `StreamingBody` failed to type-check as `ReadBuffer`/`ReadCsvBuffer`. No pandas code reads `mode` through the protocol; the only read is guarded by `hasattr` in `_is_binary_mode` (runtime support for `StreamingBody` was added in GH-52252). Removing it also makes `GzipFile` (whose `mode` is an `int` in typeshed) satisfy the protocol, so an unused `type: ignore` is dropped.

This loosens the protocol, so nothing changes at runtime. pandas-stubs has the same `mode` property and will need a matching change for most type-checker users.

### Background
Fixes #20442. Pure Python specifies that `None == None` evaluates to `True`. However, in pandas, comparing a Series of objects with scalar `None` previously short-circuited into NumPy's NA logic (treating `None` like `np.nan`), returning `False` universally for `None == None`.

### Verification
Included new unit tests covering 50+ combinations of `None` equality, including massive scale benchmarking which showed zero performance regressions. Tested against other missing datatypes (`pd.NA`, `np.nan`, `NaT`) to ensure their logic remained untouched.

Fixes #69443

## What was happening

Assigning a length-1 NumPy array into a PyArrow-backed column of a 1-row frame blew up with `TypeError: Invalid value '[5000.]' for dtype 'double[pyarrow]'`:

```python
df = pd.DataFrame({"A": pd.array([5000.0], dtype="double[pyarrow]")})
df.loc[:, "A"] = df["A"].astype(float).round(6)  # TypeError
```

The trail: `SingleBlockManager.setitem_inplace` unwraps a length-1 1-d array down to 0-d before handing it to the EA, and `ArrowExtensionArray._box_pa_scalar` then passed that 0-d array straight into `pa.scalar`, which cannot consume an ndarray. PyArrow raised `ArrowInvalid`, which surfaced as the `TypeError` above.

## The fix

In `_box_pa_scalar`, a 0-d ndarray is now unboxed to its NumPy scalar with `value[()]` before reaching `pa.scalar`. I used `[()]` rather than `.item()` deliberately: it preserves the dtype, so a `datetime64` stays a `datetime64` scalar instead of collapsing to an int. The same 0-d value also tripped `ArrowStringArray._validate_setitem_value` on its `len(value)` check, so it gets the same unboxing there and flows into the existing scalar branch. Genuinely invalid values still raise `TypeError` exactly as before.

## Tests

- New regression test `test_setitem_0d_ndarray` in `pandas/tests/extension/test_arrow.py`, covering the exact issue repro, the multi-row broadcast case (a length-1 array assigned into a 2-row frame), and the `string[pyarrow]` path.
- `pandas/tests/extension/test_arrow.py -k setitem`: 3282 passed, 42 xfailed.
- `pandas/tests/extension/test_string.py -k setitem`: all passing.
- The repro script additionally verified `int64[pyarrow]` and `timestamp[ns][pyarrow]` columns, plus that invalid values (e.g. strings into a float column) still raise `TypeError`.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on all changed files; whatsnew entry added under ExtensionArray in `v3.1.0.rst`.

## AI use

Developed through Sanjay's Muse agent (model: Muse Spark). It reproduced the issue, traced the root cause through the setitem path, drafted the fix, the regression test, and the whatsnew entry, and ran the test suites above. The diff is the complete change set: two small unboxing guards, one regression test, one whatsnew line.

```python
df.sort_index(axis=1, level="B", key=lambda x: np.argsort(index_natsorted(x)))
# KeyError: 'Level B not found'
```

`level=1` works, as does a key that returns a named `Index`. `_ensure_key_mapped_multiindex` applies the key to each level and rebuilds the `MultiIndex` with `from_arrays(mapped)`, which takes the names from the mapped arrays. A key that returns an ndarray gives an unnamed level, so `sortlevel("B")` can't find it.

As @rhshadrach suggested in the issue, the name is now set internally rather than requiring the key to return a named `Index`: the rebuilt `MultiIndex` gets `names=index.names`. `ensure_key_mapped` already wraps the key's result in an `Index`, so no other change is needed. This only affects `MultiIndex`, since `level` is a no-op on a flat index.

The test sorts by level name with a key returning an ndarray, on both axes, and fails on main. The sort tests in `tests/frame/methods`, `tests/series/methods`, `tests/indexes/multi/test_sorting.py`, `tests/test_sorting.py` and `tests/indexes/test_base.py` pass (2078 passed).

### Problem
With `MultiIndex` columns, `to_excel` wrote a NaN column label as the last value of that level (in the report, the NaN bin from `pd.cut` became `(0.0, inf]`).

### Cause
`_format_header_mi` calls `levels.take(level_codes)` without `allow_fill=True`, so the `-1` code of a NaN label wraps around to the last element. The row-index path already passes `allow_fill=True`.

`test_to_excel_multiindex_nan_column_label` runs for all engines and `merge_cells` values and reads the header rows back with `header=None`, because `read_excel` with `header=[0, 1]` forward-fills empty header cells (which is why the test in #62576 passed on `main`). Fails on `main`, passes with this change.

title: BUG: retain DatetimeIndex freq in concat regardless of input order (GH#64253)
body:
- [x] closes #64253
- [x] [Tests added and passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#writing-tests) if fixing a bug or adding a new feature
- [x] All [code checks passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#pre-commit).
- [x] Added [type annotations](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#type-hints) to new arguments/methods/functions.
- [x] Added an entry in the latest `doc/source/whatsnew/vX.X.X.rst` file if fixing a bug or adding a new feature.

### Problem

`union_indexes` combines `DatetimeIndex` inputs pairwise. When an intermediate union is not contiguous (e.g. `s1 ∪ s3` before `s2` is added), `DatetimeIndex._union` falls back to the generic set path and `_with_freq("infer")`. Inference cannot recover an offset such as `CustomBusinessDay(holidays=...)` from the values, so `freq` becomes `None` and stays `None`, making the result depend on the order of the inputs. The same path is hit by `pd.DataFrame({dict of Series})`.

The bug still reproduces on current `main`; the earlier "not replicable" comment on the issue mistook the `Pandas4Warning` about the default `sort` for the assertion failing.

### Fix

Following the review on the previous attempt (#66295): do not try to preserve `freq` at every pairwise step; validate once at the end. A private helper `_maybe_restore_freq` is called at the two points where the combined index is final (`union_indexes` "special" branch, and after `safe_sort_index` in `_get_combined_index`). It is a no-op unless the result is a monotonic `DatetimeIndex` with `freq is None` and *all* inputs are `DatetimeIndex` sharing the same non-None `freq`; in that case it runs `_validate_frequency` against the final values and re-attaches the `freq` only if they conform. Nothing is inferred, and non-conforming results (e.g. the tz-aware `America/Santiago` DST case from the issue, which has a real gap) keep `freq=None`.

### Test

`test_concat_datetimeindex_freq_order_independent` is parametrized over `sort=True/False/None` (the `None` case also asserts the existing `Pandas4Warning`). Without the fix the `True` and `None` cases fail; with it all three pass. `pandas/tests/indexes`, `frame`, `series`, `reshape`, `resample`, `tseries`, `window`, `groupby` pass locally.

title: BUG: Fix .to_latex() ValueError when table exceeds max_elements
body:
Fixes #68310

When a DataFrame exceeds the `max_elements` budget (default 262144), the Styler renderer trims rows and adds a "..." trim row. However, `_translate_latex` used `concatenated_visible_rows()` to get row indices for ctx lookups, which returned all visible rows (untrimmed). This caused a length mismatch with the trimmed `d["body"]` and raised `ValueError: zip() argument 2 is shorter than argument 1`.

**Changes:**
- Modified `_translate_body` to return `body_row_indices` (original row indices for regular rows, -1 for trim row)
- Stored `body_row_indices` in the render dict `d`
- In `_translate_latex`, use `d["body_row_indices"]` instead of `concatenated_visible_rows()`
- For trim row (r == -1), skip ctx lookups since no ctx entry exists
- Properly handle concatenated stylers by applying the same ctx offset to their body_row_indices

**Testing:**
- All 880 style tests pass
- All 156 to_latex tests pass
- All 96 format to_latex tests pass
- Verified fix works for:
  - Large frames exceeding max_elements (45211 x 6, 45211 x 17)
  - max_rows/max_columns options
  - Concatenated stylers with hidden rows and styling
  - MultiIndex, hidden rows, etc.

Fixes two off-by-a-dimension bugs in `ExponentialMovingWindow.online` that cause it to ignore the decay for single-column DataFrames, returning the unweighted cumulative mean instead of the exponentially weighted mean.

Arithmetic between a pyarrow-backed Series and a scalar now keeps the Series dtype when the scalar can be represented losslessly in that dtype, matching numpy behavior. Previously the scalar was boxed with an inferred type (int64 or double), which caused needless upcasts, e.g. int32[pyarrow] + 1 returned int64[pyarrow] and float32[pyarrow] + 1.5 returned float64[pyarrow]. title: BUG: factorize ignored use_na_sentinel on dictionary-encoded arrow arrays (#66490)
body:
- [x] closes #66490
- [x] tests added / passed
- [ ] passes `pre-commit run --all-files`
- [ ] whatsnew entry

Closes #66490.

`factorize` with default `use_na_sentinel=True` on an `ArrowDtype`-backed `pandas` object whose underlying `pyarrow.dictionary` array stored nulls as a dictionary value (`null_encoding="encode"`) returned the null inside `uniques` instead of using the `-1` sentinel. This made `use_na_sentinel` a no-op whenever the pre-encoded dictionary contained a null entry, e.g.

```python
>>> import pandas as pd, pyarrow as pa
>>> arr = pa.array(["a", "b", "c", None]).dictionary_encode(null_encoding="encode")
>>> pd.Series(arr, dtype=pd.ArrowDtype(arr.type)).factorize()
(array([0, 1, 2, 3]), Index(['a', 'b', 'c', <NA>], dtype='...'))
```

With this fix, `factorize` casts such dictionary arrays back to their value type and re-encodes with the requested null encoding so the result matches what a non-dictionary-encoded array of the same values would produce:

```python
>>> pd.Series(arr, dtype=pd.ArrowDtype(arr.type)).factorize()
(array([0, 1, 2, -1]), Index(['a', 'b', 'c'], dtype='...'))
```

title: BUG: clip with missing datetime/timedelta threshold raises TypeError
body:
Closes #44785

`Series.clip` / `DataFrame.clip` with a datetime or timedelta threshold
that contains missing values raises:

```
TypeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'Timestamp' and 'float'
```

because GH#40420 fills the missing thresholds with `±np.inf` before
comparing, and `±np.inf` cannot be compared against Timestamp or
timedelta values.

This change treats the missing positions explicitly: for datetime-like
thresholds the missing positions are tracked with a mask and the
original values are kept there (matching the documented behavior that
"a missing threshold will not clip the value"), while numeric
thresholds keep the existing `±np.inf` fill path untouched.

- Series threshold (lower/upper bound)
- DataFrame with a Series threshold along `axis=0` (rows) or `axis=1`
  (columns)
- DataFrame with a datetime-like DataFrame threshold

Regression tests added in `test_clip.py` for both Series and
DataFrame, plus a whatsnew entry.

<details>
<summary>Copy-pasteable example from the issue</summary>

```python
import pandas as pd

pd.Series([1.0, 1.0], dtype="datetime64[ns]").clip(
    pd.Series([None, 1.0], dtype="datetime64[ns]")
)
```
</details>

cc @ghost (who diagnosed the root cause in #44785)

title: PERF: Skip full array allocation in RangeIndex.isin for small query inputs
body:
- [x] closes #66263
- [x] [Tests added and passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#writing-tests) if fixing a bug or adding a new feature

- [x] Added [type annotations](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#type-hints) to new arguments/methods/functions.
- [x] Added an entry in the latest `doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst` file if fixing a bug or adding a new feature.
- [x] I have reviewed and followed all the [contribution guidelines](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/development/contributing.html)

## Summary

Implements `RangeIndex.isin` directly (GH#66263). When the query `values` are smaller than the index, the new fast path allocates only the boolean result array and checks membership with O(1) `range.__contains__`, computing the target location via `(val - start) // step`. This avoids materializing the full integer array (`self._values`, e.g. an 80MB array for a 10M-entry range) that the generic `algos.isin` path allocates.

- For `len(values) < len(self)`, use the O(1) `range.__contains__` fast path.
- For `len(values) >= len(self)`, delegate to `super().isin` as before.
- Non-sized iterables (e.g. generators) are delegated to the base implementation, preserving `Index.isin` behavior.

## Tests

Added coverage in `pandas/tests/indexes/ranges/test_range.py`:
- Correctness of the fast path across positive/negative steps, negative starts, missing values, and empty queries.
- Agreement with the materialized `Index.isin` for mixed-value queries.
- The fast path does not touch `_values` (via a monkeypatched property that raises).
- Set / non-numeric / generator inputs and the `level` kwarg.
- Fallback to the generic implementation for large queries and TypeError for non-list-like values.

title: PERF: out-of-band pickling of a sliced DataFrame (GH#55781)
body:
closes #55781

numpy serializes an ndarray out of band (PEP 574) only when it is C- or F-contiguous, so a sliced `DataFrame` — whose block values are a strided view of the parent — had its data copied into the pickle stream rather than shared with the consumer. `Block.__reduce_ex__` now makes such a block contiguous when the protocol can actually use a buffer.

The gate is `protocol >= 5` on a non-contiguous, non-object ndarray. Below protocol 5 the copy is waste: numpy copies again via `tobytes` and peak memory doubles. Object dtype numpy refuses out of band whatever the layout, as it does `datetime64`/`timedelta64` — which is why extending this to the EA-backed blocks would buy nothing. At protocol 5 peak memory is unchanged, since main already paid a `tobytes` copy on the same block, while an out-of-band consumer goes from 0 buffers to 1.

Two things worth flagging for review. The issue's own reproducer no longer shows the bug — block layout has changed since it was filed, so a column slice is already contiguous; the surviving case is the row slice, which is also the one that matters to the frameworks in the report, since they partition by rows. And the win is confined to out-of-band consumers: `pickle.dumps` defaults to protocol 4, and `to_pickle` passes no `buffer_callback`, so neither changes.

Only block values are covered. A step-sliced frame's `Index` and a `Series`' values reach the pickler by other routes and still go in band.

title: BUG: read_csv silently wrapped out-of-range integers (GH#55232)
body:
closes #55232

Since 2.0, `read_csv` silently wrapped a value the requested integer `dtype` could not hold — `read_csv(StringIO("x\n-1\n257"), dtype={"x": "UInt8"})` returned `[255, 1]` — where the `Series` and `array` constructors raise.

Three cast sites reached the wraparound:

- `_coerce_to_data_and_mask`'s `isinstance` fastpath raw-astyped instead of calling `_safe_cast`. This is the nullable half, and the actual 2.0 regression; both engines route nullable dtypes through it. Masked slots are filled before the check, since the data behind the mask is meaningless.
- the c engine's int branch in `TextReader._convert_with_dtype`. The check is gated on `user_dtype` rather than skipped for `int64`, so a column that only fits `uint64` now raises for `dtype={"x": "int64"}` instead of coming back as `uint64` with the requested dtype ignored. Inference is unaffected — it passes `user_dtype=0` and keeps the `uint64` fallback result.
- `PythonParser._cast_types`, in both branches an integer cast can reach: the plain ndarray one, and the `ExtensionArray` one that `dtype_backend="pyarrow"` lands in, because `_infer_types` applies the backend before the cast runs.

Nullable dtypes raise `TypeError`, restoring the pre-2.0 message; numpy dtypes raise `ValueError`, reusing the message the parser already produces from the fallback safe-cast block in `_convert_tokens`.

With the fastpath fixed, `BaseMaskedArray._coerce_same_family` (added in GH-66332) is redundant — both call sites fall through to the identical `_coerce_to_array(..., dtype=self.dtype)` — so it is removed. That also drops its one remaining difference, which was a bug: it checked `value._data` at masked positions, so assigning an NA whose stale payload did not fit the target dtype raised.

Deliberately unchanged: `engine="pyarrow"`, which casts the parsed frame in `_finalize_dtype` (the new parser test is `@xfail_pyarrow`); `astype`, which keeps numpy semantics and belongs to GH-45588 — note `Series`/`DataFrame` construction from an existing masked array delegates to `astype`, so only `pd.array` changes there; and float-to-integer *truncation* on the python engine, which `test_read_fwf.py::test_dtype` asserts — floats are compared truncated so only wraparound raises.

Routing the nullable path through `_safe_cast` put `IntegerDtype._safe_cast` on a hot path — it answered "is this cast safe?" by raising and catching a `TypeError`, a fixed ~5µs per call that `read_csv` pays per column per chunk. It now asks `np.can_cast(..., casting="safe")` first, which is behaviour-identical on everything that reaches it and measures 5.30µs → 1.61µs at N=10, unchanged at N=1e6 where the compare dominates.

One divergence this leaves in place, for review: on an *index* column the two engines now report an out-of-range numpy dtype differently — the c engine hits the new check (`ValueError`), while the python engine still raises `OverflowError` from `_agg_index`, which the diff does not touch. The nullable case agrees (`TypeError` on both).

This does not depend on GH-45588, which was raised on the issue as a possible prerequisite.

title: BUG: ArrowDtype timestamp setitem silently crossed the tz-aware/naive boundary
body:
Setting a tz-aware `Timestamp` into a tz-naive `timestamp[ns][pyarrow]` column stored the value's UTC epoch under a naive target, so it came back shifted by the UTC offset; the reverse direction did the same. Every `datetime64`/`DatetimeTZDtype` equivalent raises `TypeError`.

```python
arr = pd.array([1, 2, 3], dtype="timestamp[ns][pyarrow]")   # tz-naive
arr[0] = pd.Timestamp("2016-01-01 00:00", tz="US/Eastern")
arr[0]   # Timestamp('2016-01-01 05:00:00')   <- the UTC epoch stored as naive
```

`_box_pa_scalar` now raises `TypeError` when the value and the target disagree about being timezone-aware. The guard keys on `datetime`, so the `Timestamp` and plain `datetime.datetime` spellings behave alike, and there is a second guard at the trailing cast, which is where an already-boxed `pa.Scalar` reaches the boundary. Only setitem, `fillna`, `where`/`mask`, `replace` and `reindex`'s fill pass a target `pa_type`, so comparison, arithmetic and `isin` are untouched.

`ArrowDtype._get_common_dtype` stops routing a tz-aware timestamp through `numpy_dtype`, which drops the tz. This is load-bearing rather than a separate fix: without it, `Index.where`/`putmask` answer the new `TypeError` by widening through the common dtype, which collapses the index to tz-naive and silently relabels entries the caller never selected. It independently fixes `concat` and `combine_first`, which were shifting tz-aware values with no setitem involved, and the same path is what `Index.union`/`append`/`join` use — two tz-aware arrow indexes differing only in unit came back relabelled tz-naive and shifted. It also lets an unresolvable pyarrow tz label yield no common dtype rather than raising.

Deliberately out of scope: the array-valued spelling in `_box_pa_array` still crosses the boundary, since the check belongs in `_validate_setitem_value` and that reroute is GH-68419; `merge`'s key casting, `insert`/`shift(fill_value=)` via `_from_sequence`, and the lossy-unit rounding are likewise separate.

`merge_asof` accepts `tolerance=0` — an exact-match-only merge, a meaningful asof semantic — but the `MergeError` raised for a negative `tolerance` claimed the value `must be positive`. All three type-specific guards reject only strictly-negative values (`self.tolerance < 0` / `< Timedelta(0)`), so `0` passes and the "positive" wording is inconsistent with the actual constraint.

The three messages now say `tolerance must be non-negative`. A new regression test (`test_tolerance_zero`) asserts that `tolerance=0` performs an exact-match merge (a row with no exact counterpart gets no match), pinning the accepted behavior so the wording can't drift back.

title: BUG: DataFrame.replace/Series.replace silently stored a callable value
body:
`NDFrame.replace` validates `to_replace` up front but never checks `value`. A callable `value` passes straight through, so `s.replace(r"\d", lambda m: "X", regex=True)` stores the function object in the result instead of applying it or raising, and later operations on that object-dtype data fail far from the actual mistake.

```python
s = pd.Series(["a1", "b2"])
s.replace(r"\d", lambda m: "X", regex=True)
# 0    <function <lambda> at 0x...>
# 1    <function <lambda> at 0x...>
```

This adds the same kind of check that already exists for `to_replace`: `replace` now raises `TypeError` when `value` is callable, matching the error already raised for a callable `to_replace` (GH-18634). The check is recursive so it also catches a callable hiding inside a list-like or dict-like `value` (`replace([...], [callable])`, `replace({...: callable})`, `replace(regex={...: callable})`), not just a bare callable passed directly. Covered for `Series` and `DataFrame`, across all of those spellings.

Fixes #68199

This PR fixes a bug where list-indexing (and methods like `drop_duplicates`) on a `Series` subclass would lose the sequence `name` if the subclass explicitly defined its own `_metadata`.

title: BUG: PeriodIndex partial-string slicing loses anchor on same-resolution labels
body:
Fixes #66571.

Partial-string slicing on a `PeriodIndex` with an anchored freq resolves the string bound one period too early:

```python
pi = pd.period_range("2000Q1", periods=12, freq="Q-FEB")
ser = pd.Series(range(12), index=pi)
ser.loc["2001Q1":"2001Q1"]
# returns 2000Q4 and 2001Q1 instead of just 2001Q1
```

`_parsed_string_to_bounds` parses the label into a *calendar*-freq `Period` (discarding the anchor month), then converts it back with `asfreq`. When the calendar and anchored quarters don't line up, that round trip spans two periods instead of one. `get_loc` doesn't have this bug because it builds the `Period` directly from `self.freq` for this same case - reused that here.

Ran locally:
```
>>> ser.loc["2001Q1":"2001Q1"]
2001Q1    4
Freq: Q-FEB, dtype: int64
```

Also ran the full `pandas/tests/indexes/period/` suite (476 tests) plus period-related `indexing`/`truncate` tests (193 tests) - all pass.

## Summary

`Index.get_indexer` and `Index.drop` treated `pd.NA` inconsistently when matching a NaN label of a string-dtype index:

```python
idx = pd.Index([np.nan, "b"])          # str dtype

idx.get_indexer([pd.NA])                       # [0]  (matched NaN)
idx.get_indexer(np.array([pd.NA], dtype=object))  # [-1]  (bug: did not match)
idx.get_indexer(pd.Index([pd.NA]))             # [-1]  (bug: did not match)
idx.drop([pd.NA])                               # worked
idx.drop(np.array([pd.NA], dtype=object))       # KeyError (bug)
```

`Index.get_loc(pd.NA)` already matches `np.nan`, so the list-target behavior (and scalar lookup) is the intended semantics; the numpy-array and `Index` targets diverged.

Root cause: `Index._maybe_cast_listlike_indexer` normalizes missing values for a `StringDtype` (na_value `np.nan`) target — `target_index.fillna(np.nan)` — but only when the input was a plain list (`not hasattr(target, "dtype")`). Numpy arrays and `Index` objects already carry a `dtype`, so they skipped the normalization and their `pd.NA` kept a different hash than the stored `np.nan`, missing the lookup.

Fix: drop the `not hasattr(target, "dtype")` gate so array/`Index` targets are normalized too, guarded by `target_index.hasnans` (to avoid a no-op copy on NA-free targets) and excluding `MultiIndex` (whose `hasnans`/`isna` raise `NotImplementedError`).

## Verification

- Reproducer from #65419 now returns `[0]` for list, ndarray, `Index`, and `string`-dtype targets, and `drop` works for all target forms.
- Added `test_get_indexer_pd_na_matches_nan` in `pandas/tests/indexes/base_class/test_indexing.py`.
- `pytest pandas/tests/indexes/` → 18087 passed, 244 skipped, 45 xfailed.
- `pytest pandas/tests/indexes/base_class/` → 136 passed.
- `pytest pandas/tests/extension/test_string.py` → 4528 passed, 796 skipped, 20 xfailed.
- `pytest pandas/tests/reshape/` → 2903 passed, 17 skipped, 6 xfailed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on touched files → clean.

## Automated contribution disclosure

- Tool: Pi coding agent (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-coding-agent)
- Model: deepseek-v4-pro (via company-newapi)
- Reasoning-effort setting: off

The agent reproduced the inconsistency, traced it to the `not hasattr(target, "dtype")` gate in `_maybe_cast_listlike_indexer`, relaxed the gate with a `hasnans` guard and a `MultiIndex` exclusion, and wrote the regression test. I reviewed the change against the indexing code paths, verified the fix with the reproducer and the indexes/string/reshape test suites, and confirmed no regressions.

title: ENH: Add excel_sep_hint parameter to to_csv
body:
### Feature Description

Adds a new `excel_sep_hint` boolean parameter (default `False`) to `to_csv`. When `True`, prepends a `sep=<delimiter>` line before the header row in the output, which allows Microsoft Excel to automatically detect the correct delimiter when opening CSV files that use a non-comma separator (e.g. semicolons, common in European locales).

**Example:**
```python
df.to_csv('data.csv', sep=';', excel_sep_hint=True)
```

Output:
sep=;
col1;col2;col3
val1;val2;val3

Currently users have to manually prepend this line themselves before calling `to_csv`, which this makes unnecessary.

### Implementation

Threaded the parameter through the full CSV formatting chain:
- `NDFrame.to_csv` (`pandas/core/generic.py`) — added parameter to both overloads and the implementation
- `DataFrameRenderer.to_csv` (`pandas/io/formats/format.py`) — passes it through to `CSVFormatter`
- `CSVFormatter` (`pandas/io/formats/csvs.py`) — stores the flag and writes the `sep=` line in `_save()` before the header

### Tests

Added `test_excel_sep_hint` in `pandas/tests/io/formats/test_to_csv.py` verifying the output starts with the correct `sep=` line when the flag is set.

Closes #61692

## summary

- [khash_python.h](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/9f4c0ba7b0bdb9b7a2cedcf159affbcb36bf8289/pandas/_libs/include/pandas/vendored/klib/khash_python.h#L218) is silently suppressing all exceptions from `PyObject_Hash` and `PyObject_RichCompareBool`
- This is problematic because client logic might expect that exceptions thrown from their custom `__hash__` and `__eq__` methods are not silently discarded (see #57052)
- This PR implements a new layer for `pymap` that catches all exceptions thrown during khash computations and raises the exceptions properly
- Attempting to hash `dict` and `list` will result in a hash value of 0 for backwards compatibility, see below
- Fixed comparison of `pd.NA` in `pyobject_cmp`, see below
- Added wrapper on `JSONArray.duplicated` that converts `UserDict` elements to `dict` before calling `pd.core.algorithms.duplicated`.

## `dict` and `list` objects are still hashed as 0
Some existing logic, for example [core.algorithms.value_count](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/54ab8060ca2556cef803121a210a029daf2147cb/pandas/core/algorithms.py#L862), uses the `pymap` for efficiency.

High-level API examples that test this behavior:
* [`DataFrame.describe`](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/8f359f8e13a501e7f26a215796fe094825ba86bd/pandas/tests/frame/methods/test_describe.py#L355-L362)
* [`Series.isin`](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/8f359f8e13a501e7f26a215796fe094825ba86bd/pandas/tests/series/methods/test_isin.py#L254)

This was working fine because when `PyObject_Hash` would raise an exception while trying to hash unhashable keys, the error indicator was explicitly cleared, and a hash value 0 was returned. All objects would end up in the same bucket in the hashtable. Although this is not too good for performance, it is not a problem for correctness (because `pyobject_cmp` would find all objects in the bucket).

~~This PR retains that behavior for all `dict` and `list` objects. If hashing needs to be bypassed for additional types in the future, they can be added [here](https://github.com/matiaslindgren/pandas/blob/2462e30f2715650d165d1de7f232894d4fef1417/pandas/_libs/include/pandas/vendored/klib/khash_python.h#L325).~~

This PR checks if the object defines `__hash__` before calling `hash` on it. If the object is not hashable, 0 is used.


## comparing a `pandas.NA` in `pyobject_cmp` is always `False`
Exceptions were previously suppressed also in `pyobject_cmp`. One notable exception thrown during `==` comparison is when `pd.NA == x` returns `pd.NA` instead of `False/True`. ~~This PR will introduce a check for `pd.NA` and return `False` from `pyobject_cmp` when one or both of the operands are `pd.NA`.~~ This PR attempts to convert the result object from `==` into a `bool`. If that fails and/or an exception is raised during conversion, the exception is suppressed and a return value of 0 is used.

Examples:
- `1 == 1` => `True`
- `np.int64(1) == np.int64(1)` => `np.True_` => converts to `True`
- `pd.NA == pd.NA` => `bool(pd.NA)` => `TypeError` => ignored and 0 is used
- `np.array([1, 2]) == np.array([1, 2])` => `bool(np.array([True, True]))` => `ValueError` => ignored and 0 is used

title: BUG: online ewm ignoring decay for single-column frames
body:
Fixes #66522

`online_ewma` indexed `deltas` with the column index `j` instead of the row index `i`,
and `OnlineExponentialMovingWindow.mean` sized `update_deltas` from the column count
rather than the number of rows it passes to the kernel. For a single-column frame that
array is empty, so `deltas[j - 1]` is an out-of-bounds read that numba turns into
`0.0`, `old_wt_factor ** 0` is 1, and the weight never decays.

Changes:

- `online.py`: use `deltas[i - 1]`, which is the contract the comment right above the
  line already describes.
- `ewm.py`: build `update_deltas` from `len(np_array)` after `np_array` is assembled.
  The old expression was wrong on the `update=` path too, since it never accounted for
  the length of `update`; that only mattered once the kernel indexed by row.
- Added a single-column `DataFrame` to the `obj` parametrization of
  `test_online_vs_non_online_mean`. It covers both the initial `mean()` and the
  `mean(update=...)` call, and fails on main.

Verified on x86-64 Linux, CPU only, python 3.12 with numpy 2.4.6 and numba 0.66.0.
The new parametrization fails before the change and passes after; the full
`pandas/tests/window/` suite passes (9525 passed, 330 skipped, 49 xfailed). Not
verified: other numba versions, ARM or Windows, and whether the `parallel=True`
parametrizations actually ran parallelized here (numba warns it cannot parallelize
this function, and the test class filters that warning). The docs build was not run.

Thanks to @jbrockmendel for the report, which already pinned both wrong lines.

title: BUG: Fix boolean column indexer for single-column EA-backed ExtensionBlocks
body:
- [x] closes #66527
- [x] Tests added and passed
- [x] All code checks passed
- [x] Added an entry in the latest `doc/source/whatsnew/vX.X.X.rst` file
- [x] I have reviewed and followed all the contribution guidelines
- [x] If I used AI to develop this pull request, I prompted it to follow `AGENTS.md`

---

Fixes the `NotImplementedError` raised when assigning to a single-column, ExtensionArray-backed `DataFrame` with a boolean column indexer via `.loc`, e.g.:

```python
import pandas as pd

left = pd.DataFrame({"A": [f"x{i}" for i in range(60)]})
left.loc[:, left.columns.isin(["A"])] = left.loc[:, left.columns.isin(["A"])]
# NotImplementedError: This should not be reached. ...
```

### Root cause

The bug is in `ExtensionBlock._unwrap_setitem_indexer`. When the column indexer is a length-1 boolean mask (`[True]`), none of the existing branches match: the mask isn't an integer, isn't a null slice, and the positional `indexer[1][0] == 0` check fails because `np.True_ == 0` is `False`. The indexer then falls through to the `raise NotImplementedError`.

As noted on the issue, this is a long-standing latent bug rather than a 3.0-specific regression. Object-dtype columns don't hit it (`NumpyBlock._unwrap_setitem_indexer` is a no-op), and 2+ column frames don't hit it either — only single-column, EA-backed frames. pandas 3.0's default string dtype just made it much easier to trigger, since plain string columns are now EA-backed by default. It also reproduces on 2.3.x with any EA dtype (`string`, `Int64`, etc.).

### Fix

Added a branch in `ExtensionBlock._unwrap_setitem_indexer` that handles a length-1 boolean column mask selecting the single column, converting the indexer to select column 0. The branch is guarded to require the mask element be truthy, so an empty selection (`[False]`) is not incorrectly treated as selecting the column.

### Tests

Added a regression test covering `.loc` with a boolean column indexer on a single-column EA-backed `DataFrame`.

`.iloc[:, [True]]` is intentionally **not** covered: `.iloc` is positional and rejects non-integer keys, so a boolean column mask is only meaningful via `.loc`. Passing `[True]` to `.iloc` correctly raises `TypeError: Cannot index by location index with a non-integer key`, which is expected behavior and out of scope for this fix.

Ran locally:

```
python -m pytest pandas/tests/frame/indexing/test_indexing.py
```

The Period and Interval pyarrow extension types are only registered when something triggers the import of `pandas.core.arrays.arrow.extension_types`, so pyarrow reading pandas data directly gets the raw storage type back:

```python
# process 1
import pandas as pd
pd.DataFrame({"a": pd.period_range("2012", freq="Y", periods=3)}).to_parquet("p.parquet")
```

```python
# process 2, only imports pandas
import pandas
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
print(pq.read_table("p.parquet").schema.field("a").type)
# int64      <- expected extension<pandas.period<ArrowPeriodType>>
```

Reading via `pd.read_parquet` is unaffected, since `io/parquet.py` imports the module on the way. This registers the types at import time instead, behind `HAS_PYARROW`.

The two concerns raised when this was last discussed no longer apply: the circular import is gone, and pandas already imports pyarrow eagerly through `pandas.compat.pyarrow`, so registering on top of it measured ~3ms locally.

The test runs in a subprocess because registration is a process-wide side effect that other tests already trigger, so an in-process test would pass regardless of the change.

title: BUG: Fix resampling with CustomBusinessDay/BusinessDay and closed='right'
body:
Resampling with end-of-period offsets like `CustomBusinessDay` ("C") and `BusinessDay` ("B") was not correctly aligned when `closed="right"`.

In `pandas/core/resample.py` line 2701 (inside `_adjust_bin_edges`), the function only checked for specific end-of-period offsets like `"BME"`, `"ME"`, `"W"`, etc., but did not include `"B"` (BusinessDay) or `"C"` (CustomBusinessDay). When `closed="right"`, these offsets also need their bin edges rolled forward to the last moment of the day, otherwise data on the last day overflows into a new/extra bin containing `NaN` at the end and casts integer columns to `float64`.

This PR:
1. Updates `_adjust_bin_edges` to check for `"B"` and `"C"` as end-of-period offsets.
2. Adds a regression unit test `test_resample_custom_business_day` to verify correct binning and dtype preservation for `CustomBusinessDay` resampling.

Closes #65740

title: BUG: Fix NaN validity mask synchronization in FloatingArray and to_numeric (#63732)
body:
- [x] Closes #63732
- [x] Added tests for both `numpy_nullable` and `pyarrow` backends.

**Bug Description:**
The reporter and @sanrishi correctly identified a desynchronization issue where `np.nan` values were being loaded into the `FloatingArray` data payload without the corresponding boolean validity mask being updated to `True`. Because `.astype()` bypassed the constructor, `isna()` and `dropna()` were reading a "Valid" mask and completely ignoring the missing values.

**The Fix:**
1. **FIX 1:** Modified `FloatingArray.__init__` to proactively synchronize the validity mask whenever `np.nan` is detected in the incoming data payload. 
2. **FIX 2:** Updated `to_numeric` to bypass the fragile `.astype()` casting. It now explicitly routes through the official `pd.array()` constructor when `dtype_backend` is provided, ensuring correct masking during initialization.

title: BUG: Ensure consistent index naming when merging with empty DataFrames
body:
This PR fixes an inconsistency reported in #22921 where merging an empty DataFrame with a non-empty DataFrame via `left_on`/`right_index` (or `left_index`/`right_on`) inadvertently preserved the named index from the non-empty DataFrame. 

Previously, when one side was empty, `_get_join_info` bypassed standard join index creation and fell back to `copy()`/`take()` on the populated axis, dragging along its index metadata. This updates the logic to construct a fresh `default_index(n)` when one side is empty. The length `n` is correctly calculated based on the `how` parameter (e.g., `n = len(right)` for an outer join with an empty left DataFrame).

Parametrized tests have been added to ensure consistency across all join types (`inner`, `left`, `right`, `outer`).

body:

## Summary

`Series.combine` with `fill_value` gave wrong results when one Series had an integer label (e.g. `0`) absent from the other Series. Inside `combine`, `self.get(idx, fill_value)` was called, and `Series.get(0)` fell back to positional access, returning the first element instead of `fill_value`. The call `func(value, fill_value)` then produced an incorrect result.

The bug was fixed separately when `Series.__getitem__` was made strictly label-based. This PR adds a regression test so the fix is not accidentally reverted.

**Reproducer from the issue:**

```python
a = pd.Series([1, 2, 3], index=["a", "b", "c"])
b = pd.Series([10, 20, 30], index=[0, "e", "f"])
c = b.combine(a, lambda x, y: x + y, fill_value=0)
# Before fix: c[0] == 11  (0 was treated as positional, a[0]=1 was retrieved)
# After fix:  c[0] == 10  (fill_value=0 is used correctly)
```

Note: I used an automated tool (Claude Code) to help write this PR. I have reviewed the code and the test is correct.

`test_duplicated_hashtable_impl` monkeypatched `libindex._SIZE_CUTOFF` to 50, but nothing on the path under test reads it: `MultiIndex.duplicated` is `get_group_index` + `hashtable.duplicated` over the codes and never constructs an index engine. `BaseMultiIndexCodesEngine` has no `over_size_threshold` member either, so no MultiIndex engine consults the cutoff even when one is built.

This drops the `monkeypatch.context()` block and the fixture argument, renames the test to what it actually asserts — that the codes-based `MultiIndex.duplicated` agrees with `hashtable.duplicated` over the tuple values — and removes the `libindex` import, which becomes unused.

Test-only change, so no whatsnew entry. `pandas/tests/indexes/multi/test_duplicates.py` is 53 passed locally, and `pre-commit run --files` on the changed file is clean.

title: BUG: Categorical.map returns category dtype instead of bool when mapping non-bool categories to boolean values
body:
- [x] closes #61719
- [x] [Tests added and passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#test-driven-development)
- [x] All [CI checks passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_environment.html#running-the-test-suite)
- [x] Added entry in `doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst`

## Description

When mapping a `Categorical` with non-boolean categories to boolean values via `.map()`, the result incorrectly preserves `CategoricalDtype` when the mapped categories happen to be unique (e.g., single-category input). This produces inconsistent behavior depending on the number of input categories:

```python
# Single category: returns category (BUG)
pd.Series(["a", "a"]).astype("category").map(lambda x: x == "c")
# dtype: category, Categories (1, bool): [False]

# Two categories: returns bool (CORRECT)
pd.Series(["a", "b"]).astype("category").map(lambda x: x == "c")
# dtype: bool
```

## Fix

Added a condition to the categorical fast-path in `Categorical.map` that prevents preserving `CategoricalDtype` when the mapped categories have `bool` dtype but the original categories do not. This ensures boolean-valued map results consistently return `bool` dtype regardless of the number of input categories.

Boolean categoricals mapped to bool (e.g., `Categorical([True, False]).map(lambda x: not x)`) still correctly preserve categorical dtype since the original categories are already boolean.

title: BUG: ewm(adjust=False) NaN gaps disagree for times vs no-times
body:
- [ ] closes #66523 (blocked on `Needs Discussion` / `/take`; xref until the label is removed)
- [x] also addresses #31178 (same root cause: `new_wt = 1 - old_wt` used accumulated decay)
- [x] [Tests added and passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#writing-tests) if fixing a bug or adding a new feature
- [x] All [code checks passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#pre-commit).
- [x] Added [type annotations](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#type-hints) to new arguments/methods/functions.
- [x] Added an entry in the latest `doc/source/whatsnew/vX.X.X.rst` file if fixing a bug or adding a new feature.
- [x] I have reviewed and followed all the [contribution guidelines](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/development/contributing.html)
- [x] If I used AI to develop this pull request, I prompted it to follow `AGENTS.md`.

AI: Grok 4.6 (Grok Build).

`adjust=False` special-cased `com == 1` as `new_wt = 1 - old_wt` (GH-59142). That is the right convex weight when `old_wt` is just this step's decay. After an `ignore_na=False` NaN row, `old_wt` has already been multiplied, so the new observation absorbs the entire forgotten mass:

- 3.0 regression on the no-`times` path for `com=1` (GH-31178: `4.0` instead of `11/3`)
- the same wrong value on the `times` path, which always forces `_com = 1.0`

The intended split, from the documented `ignore_na=False` recursion, GH-59142's irregular-interval tests, and `test_ewma_with_times_equal_spacing`, is:

- each *row-to-row* interval is one step of length `δ`
- weight the new observation by that step only: `new_wt = 1 - (1-α)^δ` (`δ = 1` without `times`)
- leave decay accumulated across NaN rows in `old_wt` and renormalize
- `ignore_na=True` skips the step that lands on a null; it is not "dropna and keep the calendar gap" (that reading would make equally spaced `times` return `4.0` instead of the no-times `3.0`)

The cython `mean` path now always receives `_deltas` (all ones when `times` is omitted), so times and no-times share one decay formula. Equally spaced `times` match no-`times` for every `adjust` / `ignore_na` combination, including on NaN data. `test_ewma_with_times_variable_spacing` is unchanged (`0.2376251864…`).

A mixed case (NaN row, then a 2-day jump) distinguishes the three candidates:

- this PR: `31/7`
- convex over the accumulated gap: `4.5`
- one normalized Δ=3 step: `4.2`

title: ENH: Add transparent JIT compilation engine support to Series.apply
body:
### Description

This PR implements native JIT compilation for User-Defined Functions (UDFs) passed to `Series.apply()`, adopting the "Predictable by Default, Scalable by Configuration" strategy.

Resolves #66281 

### Proposed Changes
1. **Series.apply API**: Added `engine` and `engine_kwargs` parameters to `Series.apply()`, which are forwarded to the `SeriesApply` constructor.
2. **JIT Helpers & Caching**: Added helper routines in `pandas/core/util/numba_.py`:
   - `global_numba_apply_loop`: A thread-parallelized JIT loop compiled dynamically based on UDF signature and cached to avoid recompilation costs.
   - `maybe_run_numba_apply`: Filters series size (threshold set to 50k for auto-JIT) and checks dtype compatibility (numeric/datetime/timedelta) before attempting to JIT compile.
   - `_JIT_APPLY_CACHE`: Modules-level lookup table storing compiled functions.
3. **Apply Engine Dispatch**: Modified `SeriesApply.apply_standard` in `pandas/core/apply.py` to route execution through `maybe_run_numba_apply` prior to mapping values.
4. **Unit Tests**: Added `pandas/tests/apply/test_numba_apply.py` verifying correctness, explicit opt-in, global options, and error boundaries.

### Benchmarks (1,000,000 elements, numeric series)
* **Standard Interpreter apply**: `0.872` seconds
* **JIT apply (first run with compile time)**: `1.083` seconds
* **JIT apply (cached subsequent run)**: `0.037` seconds
* **Cached Speedup Factor**: **23.42x**

title: BUG: merge key dtype differs between symmetric how='left'/how='right' calls
body:
- [x] closes #56454
- [x] [Tests added and passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#writing-tests) if fixing a bug or adding a new feature
- [x] All [code checks passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#pre-commit).
- [x] Added [type annotations](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#type-hints) to new arguments/methods/functions.
- [x] Added an entry in the latest `doc/source/whatsnew/vX.X.X.rst` file if fixing a bug or adding a new feature.
- [x] I have reviewed and followed all the [contribution guidelines](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/development/contributing.html)
- [x] If I used AI to develop this pull request, I prompted it to follow `AGENTS.md`.

`a.merge(b, on="key", how="left")` and `b.merge(a, on="key", how="right")` describe the same logical join, but the shared key column's dtype depended on which frame `.merge()` was called on, not on `how`. `_get_merge_keys` always drops the shared join-key column from `self.right` and keeps it from `self.left`, regardless of `how`. `_maybe_add_join_keys` normally reconciles this via `find_common_type` when there are missing/unmatched rows to fill, but when every row already lines up 1:1 (both `left_indexer` and `right_indexer` are `None`), that reconciliation step is skipped entirely, so the output silently kept `self.left`'s dtype even for a right join.

This adds a narrowly-scoped case: only when `how == "right"` and no reindexing is needed on either side, use the right frame's original key array/dtype (mirroring how a left join already keeps the left frame's dtype in that same situation). `how="right"` merges that do need reindexing/filling are untouched and continue to go through the existing `find_common_type` reconciliation path unchanged.

One existing test (`test_merge_ea_and_non_ea`) asserted the old (buggy) behavior for `how="right"` and has been updated to reflect the corrected, symmetric dtype.

AI disclosure: I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to investigate the root cause, implement this fix, and write the tests/whatsnew entry. I reviewed, tested, and take responsibility for the change.

title: DOC: repair stale pandas.pydata.org documentation links
body:
Supersedes the closed GH-66599, which fixed one of these links by dropping `/dev/` from the URL.

This repairs every hardcoded `pandas.pydata.org` link in `pandas/` that points at a page `doc/redirects.csv` redirects. The doc site serves those as a stub that `doc/make.py` writes as `content="0;URL={target}.html"` — with no fragment — so any `#anchor` is silently dropped and the reader lands at the top of the target page. A link checker cannot see this: the status is 200, and fragments are not validated.

**Legacy pre-`user_guide/` paths** (5). `pandas-docs/stable/{io,groupby,indexing}.html`. Three carry a fragment that the stub drops: `#io-chunking` (the `read_csv`/`read_table` `chunksize` docs, twice) and `#attribute-access` (the `__setattr__` warning). The two `groupby.html` links resolve, but through the legacy path.

**Pages consolidated into the migration guide by GH-63971** (31). `user_guide/copy_on_write` and `user_guide/migration-3-strings` are both `redirects.csv` sources now, so these move to `user_guide/migration.html`: the three CoW warning strings in `pandas/errors/cow.py`, the 27 `copy=` docstring links pointing at the CoW guide, and the `select_dtypes` `Pandas4Warning`. The 27 are already stubs today; the other four break at the next release. The `cow.py` messages keep their `#chained-assignment` / `#copy-on-write-cow` anchors, which the stub would drop. The 27 docstring links stay fragmentless, as they were before — with an anchor they exceed the 88-column limit, and wrapping a URL across two lines spoils it for anyone reading the docstring verbatim.

Everything stays on `docs/dev/`: `docs/user_guide/migration.html` is a 404 until 3.1 ships, so the dev docs are the only spelling that works both now and after the release.

Also removes the now-unused `linkcheck_ignore` entry for `stable/io.html#io-chunking` in `conf.py`, and converts two hardcoded URLs in `.rst` files to `:ref:` — the last two hardcoded spellings of those targets under `doc/source`. `:ref:` is deliberately not used in docstrings, per review: a Sphinx role is not useful to anyone reading a docstring verbatim in a terminal, notebook or IDE. The rewrite of the links that already resolved is dropped too, also per review.

Every URL in the diff was resolved: 200, not a redirect stub, and where it has a fragment, the anchor id confirmed present in the served HTML.

On the suggestion in GH-45409: a link-check cron is complementary to this, not a substitute. It catches hard 404s; every link in this PR returns 200. Worth noting that `.github/workflows/broken-linkcheck.yml` no longer exists, so `linkcheck_ignore` is currently configuration nothing exercises.

title: DEPR: Timestamp.timestamp treating tz-naive as UTC (GH#50298)
body:
closes #50298

`Timestamp.timestamp()` interprets a tz-naive `Timestamp`'s wall clock as UTC, while `datetime.datetime.timestamp()` interprets a naive `datetime` as local time. Since `Timestamp.fromtimestamp()` delegates to the stdlib, the two disagree with each other: `Timestamp.fromtimestamp(x).timestamp() != x` in any non-UTC zone.

This deprecates the tz-naive behavior with a `Pandas4Warning`. No returned value changes here; enforcement (naive interpreted as local time, matching the stdlib) would be the 4.0 step, and `ts.tz_localize("UTC").timestamp()` preserves the current behavior. Follow-up to GH-65423, which documented the divergence and was closed in favor of resolving it.

Worth flagging: enforcement would make a naive `.timestamp()` depend on the machine's local timezone, and pandas treats naive datetimes as "no timezone" rather than "local" everywhere else. The counterweight is that `Timestamp` is a `datetime` subclass whose two stdlib-named epoch methods currently contradict each other.

title: BUG: defer the blocked-numexpr warning to first use (GH#66956)
body:
Follow-up to GH-66956, addressing @jorisvandenbossche's review comment there: that PR warned about the refused numexpr 2.14.1 at `import pandas`, which reaches users who never evaluate anything through numexpr — including the many who have it transitively, since PyTables hard-depends on it.

The warning now fires at most once per process, at the first operation that would actually have been offloaded: arithmetic and comparisons large enough and of the right dtype for numexpr, `where`/`mask`, and `eval`/`query` on the default engine. A small `df + df` stays silent, and so does everything when `compute.use_numexpr` is False. `expressions.py` gains `_evaluate_blocked`/`_where_blocked`, chosen by `set_use_numexpr` only when the option is on and the installed numexpr is blocked; they gate on the same `_can_use_numexpr` predicate the numexpr path uses, so "would have used numexpr" cannot drift from the real decision.

An explicit `engine="numexpr"` still raises `ImportError` rather than warning. Since that path no longer has a warning alongside it, the message now names the refused version instead of telling a user who does have numexpr installed that it "is not installed".

HDF5 `where=` queries remain uncovered, as the whatsnew already states, because PyTables imports numexpr itself. The warning is deliberately not raised there: its text says numexpr "will not be used by pandas", which is false on that path, and making it accurate would need a second message and a second one-shot flag.

The GH-66956 whatsnew bullet is amended in place rather than given its own entry, since 3.1 is unreleased.

title: BUG: iloc setitem wrote the wrong cells on a Copy-on-Write referenced frame (GH#65446)
body:
Repairs a regression from GH-65864, which is in 3.0.4 and later.

When another object references a `DataFrame`'s values, `BlockManager.setitem` splits the block so only the targeted columns get copied, then re-expresses the caller's column indexer in the new block's coordinates. GH-65864 collapsed any increasing column selection to `slice(None)` and compensated for reordered ones with an array of positions, plus a reshape of the row indexer to `(n, 1)`. Both substitutions change what numpy does: a slice takes the cross product with the row indexer, an array broadcasts against it. So the referenced path could disagree with the unreferenced one in either direction — writing a cross product where the caller asked for an elementwise pairing, or the other way round.

The column indexer now keeps the kind the caller used: an integer stays an integer, a slice stays a slice (reversed if the selection was), `Ellipsis` normalizes to `slice(None)` since it also selects the axis in full, and anything else stays an array of positions. The row-indexer reshape goes with it — it was independently wrong, turning an intended broadcast into a cross product whenever `np.ix_` had not already run — and so does the `np.squeeze`, which is only correct for `np.ix_` output; a user-supplied 2-D row key still reaches that spot, and not squeezing it is what makes it match the unreferenced path.

Symptoms fixed, all only when another object holds a reference:

```python
df = pd.DataFrame(np.arange(12.0).reshape(4, 3), columns=list("abc"))
ref = df[["a", "b", "c"]]

df.iloc[[2, 0], ::-1] = np.array([100.0, 101.0, 102.0])
# IndexError: shape mismatch: indexing arrays could not be broadcast
#   together with shapes (2,) (3,)

df.iloc[np.array([1, 0]), range(1, -1, -1)] = 99.0
# silently writes 4 cells; without the reference it writes 2

df.loc[np.array([True, False, True, False]), "c":"a":-1] = 99.0
# IndexError: too many indices for array: array is 2-dimensional, but 3 were indexed
```

For the `managers.py` split path the unreferenced path is the oracle: it never enters this code, so referenced-vs-unreferenced is a differential with no shared failure mode. Over 35,728 cases (4 dtypes x 4 frame shapes x 20 row-key spellings x 14 column-key spellings x 7 value shapes, `iloc` and `loc`) `main` diverges in 3,621. The branch's residual divergences are the empty-indexer family, where an early return skips value validation; that predates GH-65864 and is left alone here.

`EABackedBlock.setitem` needed a second change, and it is not covered by that oracle. Keeping the column indexer as an array walks 2-D EA blocks into the `indexer[::-1]` + `value.T` pair, which `slice(None)` had been keeping them out of. Two advanced indices broadcast against each other, and their order does not change the result's orientation, so the `value.T` is spurious there; it is now gated accordingly. Because the unreferenced path always reached that pair through `np.ix_`, the gate also changes **unreferenced** all-`datetime64`/`timedelta64` frames: `df.iloc[[2, 0], [0, 2]] = value` with a 2-D value silently wrote the transposed cells, and a non-square selection raised `OutOfBoundsDatetime`. There the oracle is the float64 peer, which both now match. Hence the second whatsnew entry.

Note for the backport decision: GH-65864 shipped in 3.0.4, so the `IndexError`/`ValueError` families here are live for 3.0.x users. The datetimelike entry is *not* a GH-65864 regression — `value = value.T` came in with GH-64620 (2026-03-15), and the unreferenced path never enters the block GH-65864 changed — so a backport necessarily carries that older fix too. The entry is in `v3.1.0.rst` as there is no open 3.0.x file (3.0.6 released 2026-09-17).

Overlap with GH-68521: that PR rewrites the same `EABackedBlock.setitem` hunk, and its second whatsnew entry describes the same 2-D-value transposition fixed here, with a more general `transposed` flag that also handles a 1-D value. Whichever lands first, the other should drop the duplicate entry and rebase onto it.
